quote: Euler formally introduced the famous 'thirty-six officers problem' around 1779, which was published in 1782. Unable to find a solution for a 6 square, Euler conjectured that no group based Graeco-Latin squares could exist if the order was an odd multiple of two.
note: Euler's thirty-six officers problem and his conjecture about Graeco-Latin squares represent the earliest formally posed mathematical problems about Latin squares with a documented date. The problem was presented around 1779 and formally published in 1782 in 'Recherches sur une nouvelle espèce de quarrés magiques'. While Ozanam published a recreational card puzzle involving orthogonal Latin squares in 1725, Euler's work represents the first formal mathematical conjecture and open problem in the field.
